summary: 66-year-old smoker with occupational exposure and two episodes of painless visible haematuria, culture negative, Hb 13.4.

inputs.hpi: Two episodes of painless red urine in 3 weeks, the last with small clots. No dysuria, no frequency, no loin pain. Urine culture from the GP was negative. Smoker, 40 pack-years. Worked in a rubber factory for 20 years.

exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no masses, bladder not palpable. PR: small benign prostate.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Urological cancers: refer using a suspected cancer pathway (2-week wait) for bladder or kidney cancer if aged ≥45 with unexplained visible haematuria without urinary tract infection, or visible haematuria that persists or recurs after successful treatment of UTI; suspected spinal metastases in people with cancer
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (updated).

guideline.name: EAU Guidelines on Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer (diagnosis)
guideline.section: Visible haematuria: cystoscopy and upper tract imaging (CT urography); haematuria in patients on anticoagulant or antiplatelet treatment is investigated in the same way
guideline.citation: Gontero P, Birtle A, Compérat E, et al. EAU Guidelines on Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer (TaT1 and CIS). EAU Guidelines Office, Arnhem; 2024 edition.

rationale: NICE NG12: age ≥45 with unexplained visible haematuria → suspected cancer pathway; cystoscopy and upper-tract imaging (EAU).
